_comment: "When this attacks, you may banish a card with 1{p} from each hero's graveyard. If you do, this gets +1{p}, then repeat this process." The previous version had no MAY and hung MODIFY_ATTACK off the trigger as a SIBLING of the banish, so the pump applied whether or not anything was banished and whether or not the player wanted it -- the card was strictly stronger than printed, and 'if you do' was not modelled at all. It read 0/25 against the spectator corpus and 1/3 against built states (delta +1 on every unpaid row). Three separate pieces are needed and each is now explicit. (1) EACH HERO'S GRAVEYARD is two banishes, SELF and OPPONENT, not one: with only our side drained the cost was never really paid. (2) 'If you do' gates the pump on the banish actually happening, via the `banished` ref BANISH sets -- REF_EXISTS is the same shape tricorn_of_saltwater_death uses for its WateryGrave discard. Both banishes must land, so the CONDITIONAL tests the ref after both. (3) 'Then repeat this process' is a real REPEAT, added to the DSL for this: the alternative was unrolling N copies, which silently truncates the card in the games where the loop matters. The loop's `while` re-checks that both graveyards still hold a 1-power card, so it ends when either runs dry; STOP_REPEAT in the MAY's else-branch ends it when the player declines, which is what 'you may' means for the second and later passes. `max` is the DSL's hard bound and is unreachable here -- a graveyard runs out long before 50. Talishar agrees on both branches: 1 declined, 2 taken with one 1-power card in each graveyard.
